samples.summary: `sheets import`'s new cell-table mode has no command-level test — only the pure helpers are covered
samples.evidence: The command gained: `isCellTable(rows)` selecting `buildCellMapFromTable` over `buildCellMap`, `--start` silently becoming inert in that branch, a new `mode: 'cells' | 'grid'` field merged into the response (sheets-import.ts:103-123), and `parseOutputFormat` moved ahead of the request (line 60). `packages/cli/test/csv-parse.test.ts` tests `isCellTable`/`buildCellMapFromTable` in isolation, but nothing drives `registerSheetsImportCommand`. Nothing would fail if the command called `buildCellMap` in both branches, or omitted `mode` from the emitted result, or reported `mode: 'grid'` for a cell table — exactly the wiring class of bug the diff's own `sheets export` schema-parity test was added to catch. `registry.ts` now advertises `mode` to agents with no test that it is emitted.
searchedFor: Grep 'registerSheetsImportCommand|sheets.*import' over packages/cli/**/*.test.ts → only csv-parse, files-upload, namespaces, schema (name-registry assertions only)
read packages/cli/test/sheets-export.test.ts (export got a wiring test; import did not)

samples.summary: Assertions inside the mocked `open()` callback are swallowed by login.ts's catch, so they cannot fail the test
samples.evidence: `login.ts:54-59` wraps `await open(oauthUrl)` in `try { … } catch { /* Browser open failed */ }`. The test's `open` mock awaits `onOpen(url)`, and `onOpen` contains `expect(res.status).toBe(200)` / `expect(forged.status).toBe(403)` / `expect(real.status).toBe(200)`. A failing expect there throws into that catch and is discarded — the test does not fail on those assertions. They happen to be backstopped by the outer `exchangeBodies`/`onRefusal` checks, but as written they are dead assertions, and a throw before the genuine fetch turns a real regression into an opaque vitest timeout rather than a named failure.

samples.summary: Only one of the four security headers the confirmation page sets is asserted
samples.evidence: The middleware sets `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'`, `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:108-112). The spec asserts only `X-Frame-Options`. Dropping the CSP fallback (which is what modern browsers honour for framing), the no-store (a cached confirmation page leaks the one-time secret to the next user of a shared browser) or the referrer policy would not fail any test.

samples.summary: `renderConfirmPage`'s HTML escaping is never exercised by a test
samples.evidence: `escapeHtml` is new code and the function doc explicitly says the page 'must stay inert even if a future caller loosens one of those parsers' (lines 117-127). Every test feeds already-constrained values (`port '49152'`, hex nonce, 43-char challenge, a base64url secret), so no assertion would fail if `escapeHtml` were replaced with the identity function. The `href` test even strips `&` back out rather than asserting the escaping happened. A direct `renderConfirmPage(49152, undefined, 'a"><script>', undefined)` style test would pin it.

samples.summary: `cliStateCookieName()` / `cliStateCookieOptions()` have no production `__Host-`/Secure/Path test, unlike their two siblings
samples.evidence: `oauth-state.spec.ts` covers `oauthStateCookieName`/`oauthStateCookieOptions` under NODE_ENV=production, and the middleware spec covers the confirm cookie's `__Host-` prefix, but nothing covers the CLI state cookie's name or options in production. The controller/guard tests call `cliStateCookieName()` to build their fixtures, so they are tautological with respect to the name and pass under any value. Losing `secure`, `path: '/'` or the prefix on this cookie — the binding the whole 'carried into another browser' defence rests on — fails no test.

samples.summary: No test asserts the CLI state cookie is cleared (single-use) on the callback
samples.evidence: The web flow got `expect(res.clearCookie).toHaveBeenCalledWith('wafflebase_oauth_state', …)` (auth.controller.spec.ts:407). The CLI branch performs the equivalent `res.clearCookie(cliStateCookieName(), …)` at auth.controller.ts:180-183, and none of the five CLI-flow tests assert it — removing that clear (leaving a replayable browser binding cookie behind) would keep the suite green.
searchedFor: read CLI-flow describe block in full

samples.evidence: `loginErrorUrl` strips trailing slashes from `FRONTEND_URL` (`.replace(/\/+$/, '')`), but the spec's ConfigService mock returns `'http://localhost:5173'` with no trailing slash (auth.controller.spec.ts:38), so all four LOGIN_ERROR_URL assertions pass identically with the `replace` deleted. A configured `FRONTEND_URL=http://x/` would produce `http://x//login?error=…` and nothing catches it.
searchedFor: read loginErrorUrl and the web-flow describe

samples.summary: No test that `CliLoginConfirmMiddleware` is actually registered for GET /auth/github
samples.evidence: `AuthModule.configure` is new wiring, and the guard spec's 'mints no CLI state for an unconfirmed CLI request' test proves only the failure mode if it is unwired (every CLI login silently degrades to a browser login and no CLI ever completes). Nothing asserts `consumer.apply(CliLoginConfirmMiddleware).forRoutes({ path: 'auth/github', method: GET })` — a wrong path or method there breaks CLI login entirely with a green suite. Neither the middleware spec (constructs the class directly) nor the guard spec (sets `__cliConfirmed` by hand) exercises the registration.

samples.summary: The `state.mode !== 'cli'` rejection path in the callback is untested
samples.evidence: `consumeState` returns the stored `mode`, and the controller only proceeds when `state.mode === 'cli'`, otherwise throwing the 'different browser' BadRequest (auth.controller.ts:185, 218). `cli-auth.store.spec.ts` creates `'browser'`-mode states, but no controller test presents a valid non-CLI-mode state token with its matching cookie, so the guard clause could be deleted without failing anything.

samples.summary: `expect(html).toContain('Continue')` is satisfied by the page heading regardless of whether the Continue link exists
samples.evidence:
The rendered page's `

` is 'Continue signing in to the Wafflebase CLI?', so this assertion holds even if the `Continue` were removed entirely. The following `confirm=${secret}` assertion carries the real weight; the 'Continue' check adds nothing.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: sheets-import.ts:103-123 adds cell-table branch selection (isCellTable -> buildCellMapFromTable vs buildCellMap), an inert --start in that branch, and a new agent-visible `mode: 'cells'|'grid'` field merged into the emitted result, which registry.ts:569-572 documents as part of the response contract. No test anywhere drives this command: repo-wide grep for registerSheetsImportCommand finds only sheets.ts:16 and archived docs; every test that calls parseAsync (cells, tabs, output, sheets-export, files-format, api-keys, schema, namespaces, status, login-command) passes only 'sheets cells/tabs/export/get' argv, never 'import'; the backend CLI round-trip e2e suite covers docs/notes/slides import but has no sheets counterpart; there are no colocated packages/cli/src *.test.ts files; scripts/agent/charters/round-trip.md:15 is prose, not a test; and schema.test.ts has zero 'mode' assertions. csv-parse.test.ts:123-171 covers only the pure helpers, so nothing would fail if the command used buildCellMap in both branches or omitted/mislabeled `mode`.
